why: A cartoon meeting room as people leave. Nina stops by Theo's seat; her comment appears as a speech bubble between them.
Same room, a week later. Theo at the screen, slides stacking up; the budget question slide sits last and the wall clock is past the hour.
The speech bubble drifts to an everyday desk where a figure seen from behind reads the same kind, empty comment on their screen.
The vague bubble beside an empty target board with no dart on it: a warm glow on one side, nothing to aim at on the other.
The presenter beside the paused meeting scene, gesturing to Nina's bubble as if inviting the viewer to work on it together.
A tag reading You ramble slaps onto Theo's chest. Theo folds his arms and leans back; a thin wall rises between him and Nina.
The label peels off Theo. Nina's bubble rewrites itself into the behaviour line while a small replay of Tuesday's slide stack shows the budget slide arriving last.
The behaviour line holds still with two empty dashed slots after it, pulsing gently while the viewer thinks.
The first dashed slot fills with the effect line. Beside it a wall calendar flips and the budget decision card slides from this week to next.
The second slot fills with the step. Nina and Theo turn toward each other at the table; Theo nods and adds a note of his own to it.
The complete comment sits large, its three parts lighting up in three calm colours as each is said; the old vague bubble is a faint ghost behind it.
A report arriving in an inbox on Friday night, then three answer cards sliding in one at a time as each is read, none marked.
Card B lifts forward and gains three ticks in the same three colours as Nina's comment.
Card C with two ticks and an empty third slot circled; card A with no ticks at all.
A sticky note on a monitor with a vague comment; it is crossed out and three empty coloured slots appear beneath it, ready to fill.
The opening meeting room again: the budget slide now first in Theo's stack, hands raised to decide, the clock well before the hour; Nina's three-colour comment small in the corner.
